newsitem.title: CHILE: Codelco Radomiro Tomic sees start-up before Dec.
newsitem.headline: Codelco Radomiro Tomic sees start-up before Dec.

text.p: Building work at Chilean state copper company Codelco's Radomiro Tomic mine is ahead of schedule and the pit may start producing copper up to three months earlier than planned, said a top official.
"With all the advances registered to date, we assume that production will begin before December," Luis Farias, general manager of Radomiro Tomic, told Reuters.
"(Production) could start two or three months earlier than planned."
Codelco, the world's largest copper producer, had expected to begin production at the mine in late 1997.
Farias said that construction work was running ahead of schedule at the mine which was due to take around two years to build.
"Progress has been significant. The mine has achieved an advance of 133 percent in work scheduled from the first moment until now," he said.

The $640 million mine will produce 150,000 tonnes of copper cathodes a year using heap-leaching technology to exploit oxide mineral reserves. It may be expanded in a second stage to at least 225,000 tonnes.
Radomiro Tomic lies in the Atacama Desert, a stone's throw from the corporation's giant Chuquicamata mine.
For Codelco, created in 1971 with the nationalization of mines belonging to two North American companies, it will be the first time the corporation has built a new mine from scatch.
The low-cost heapleaching technology will mean Radomiro Tomic will have cash production costs of $0.38 a pound, below costs at Codelco's other four divisions, officials have said.
